note: Faithful rendering of the root verse, its gloss, the 'statement open to attack' argument and the Sāṃkhya/Vaiśeṣika example; only minor looseness (e.g. 'even in the slightest').

errors.english: the world they protected has been utterly destroyed and exhausted
errors.why: The world-protector as Protector is the Buddha; it is the blind beings bereft of him who are ruined and wearied, not a world 'they protected'.

errors.english: What else could now be destroyed?
errors.why: The verse laments that even he whose foot-dust was supreme on the bowed heads of the gods has now perished; it is not a rhetorical 'what else could be destroyed'.

note: A readable prose rendering of the lament verses, largely accurate, with two verses misconstrued.
The Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva, Prajñāpāramitā and Cārvāka citations are correctly rendered and the argument against the charge of nihilism is clear.

errors.english: spoken for the purpose of guiding beings
errors.why: drang ba'i don is neyārtha: the three-vehicle teaching was spoken as provisional meaning, not 'for guiding beings'.

fix.find: spoken for the purpose of guiding beings

errors.english: Manjushri, the division of vehicles one line of text not transcribed
errors.why: The side simply ends mid-sentence ('Mañjuśrī, the [establishing of] vehicles…'); nothing is missing, so the unmarked claim of an untranscribed line is spurious.

fix.find: Manjushri, the division of vehicles one line of text not transcribed

note: Lotus-sūtra verses and the Satyakaparivarta citation are well rendered, but neyārtha is lost and a bogus transcription remark is appended.

errors.english: This famine lasts for a year, a month, and seven days.
errors.why: The famine lasts seven years, seven months and seven days (as in the Abhidharmakośa), not one year and one month.

fix.find: This famine lasts for a year, a month, and seven days.
fix.replace: This famine lasts for seven years, seven months and seven days.

errors.english: of the period of the abiding of those who are attached
errors.why: chags pa here is the formed world (vivṛtta): this is the first intermediate aeon of the abiding of what has formed, not of 'those who are attached'.

fix.find: of the period of the abiding of those who are attached
fix.replace: of the period of abiding of the world that has formed

errors.english: They search through houses with the tips of sticks for any small bit of food.
errors.why: This is the 'tally-stick' famine (śalākā): provisions are allotted within households by tally sticks ('today the master eats, tomorrow the mistress'), not searched for with sticks.

errors.english: Thus, the formation of the world lasts for twenty intermediate aeons.
errors.why: The text lists four twenty-aeon periods (formation, the formed world abiding twenty, destruction, the destroyed world remaining twenty) making eighty; the English folds abiding into formation and emptiness into destruction, leaving only forty.

note: The cosmological sequence is mostly followed, but the famine duration, the 'abiding' period and the tally-stick famine are mistranslated.

errors.english: If one thinks that the author's own intended position constitutes what is refuted in treatises, but not its auxiliary limbs
errors.why: bzlog pa here is exclusion (vyavaccheda): the inclusion of 'own' and 'intended' in the treatises serves to exclude something, which is not the function of a member of the proof; nothing is 'refuted'.

errors.english: merely the crown nature [note: essential summit]
errors.why: spyi bo'i is almost certainly a corruption of spyi'i, 'the general form'; 'crown nature / essential summit' is meaningless here.

note: A dense Nyāya-logic lemma commentary rendered literally and often opaquely; the lemma structure is kept but key terms (exclusion, general form) are misread.

errors.english: Good Conduct [note: original: Norzang] likewise entered into and remained in the position of a minister of excellent conduct.
errors.why: Nor bzang is the prince Sudhana, not Good Conduct; Sudhana installed Good Conduct (legs pa'i brtul zhugs) as minister.

fix.find: Good Conduct [note: original: Norzang] likewise entered into and remained in the position of a minister of excellent conduct.
fix.replace: Norzang (Sudhana, the prince), for his part, installed Good Conduct in the position of minister.

errors.why: Those of good conduct attended on Norzang (Sudhana), not on Good Conduct.

errors.english: By what means can I send this Good Conduct to another birth
errors.why: Noble Lineage plots the death of Norzang (Sudhana) himself, the youth bound to the kinnarī, not of Good Conduct.

fix.find: By what means can I send this Good Conduct to another birth
fix.replace: By what means can I send Norzang (Sudhana) himself to another birth

errors.english: she pretended to sleep [note: original: {fake, sleep}], and I was busily gazing upon her face
errors.why: The narrative is third-person: one feigned sleep while the other gazed at his/her face; there is no 'I', and the roles are likely reversed (the prince feigns sleep, she gazes, he suddenly opens his eyes and laughs).
smyon chu is the rut-fluid (mada) of elephants in musth, not water.

note: The courtship verses are passable, but the translator conflates the prince Norzang (Sudhana) with the brahmin Good Conduct, so the plot of the plot against Sudhana is misattributed throughout.

errors.english: If sin were the cause or the pervasive quality of heaviness
errors.why: khyab bya is the pervaded (vyāpya), not the pervader; the argument turns on lightness being opposed to the effect or to the pervader (heaviness).

fix.find: If sin were the cause or the pervasive quality of heaviness
fix.replace: If sin were the cause of heaviness or what is pervaded by heaviness

errors.english: it is in contradiction with the abandonment of heaviness, not with the sin itself
errors.why: The Tibetan says that because it removes heaviness, it is opposed to heaviness, not to sin; it is not 'in contradiction with the abandonment of heaviness'.

note: The critique of initiation removing sin is followed in outline, but the logical vocabulary (pervaded/pervader) and one contradiction relation are garbled.
The discussion of whether sense activity grasps universals and particulars, the opponent's view and its refutation are accurately rendered.

errors.english: whatever does not depend on the essence of something is determined not to have that essence
errors.why: The principle is that whatever is independent of anything else for a given nature is necessarily determined to have that nature; the English inserts a negation.

fix.find: whatever does not depend on the essence of something is determined not to have that essence
fix.replace: whatever does not depend on anything else for a given nature is necessarily determined to have that nature

errors.english: The example invalidating valid cognition stated as
errors.why: This is the example of an invalidating valid cognition (bādhaka-pramāṇa), not an example that invalidates valid cognition.

fix.find: The example invalidating valid cognition stated as
fix.replace: The example of an invalidating valid cognition (bādhaka-pramāṇa), stated as

note: The lemma structure of the commentary on momentariness is followed, but the key independence principle is inverted and bādhaka-pramāṇa is misconstrued.
